source_evidence.observation: The paper studies Ax=b with n equations in n unknowns over a floating-point subset of the reals. Relative roundoff is bounded by u>0 with n*u <= 0.01; referenced floating-point results are assumed well defined; array absolute values and inequalities are componentwise.
Only absolute vector norms are considered: || |v| ||=||v||, equivalently monotonicity under componentwise domination. The norm is normalized by ||e_j||=1 and extended to row vectors and matrices.
The paper defines kappa(A^-1)=|| |A| |A^-1| || and warns that this is not a standard norm-based condition number.
Lower-case c_j and upper-case C_j denote scalar and matrix quantities, respectively, which the paper calls positive and bounded above by functions of n only.

A column-pivoted solve for x=A^-1 b satisfies |A x_hat-b| <= u C_2 |A| |x| when c_1*u*kappa(A^-1) <= 1/2, where c_1=||C_1|| and C_2=(I-u C_1|A||A^-1|)^-1 C_1. The preceding certificate is |A x_hat-b| <= u C_1|A||x_hat| with C_1 nonnegative.

The initial x_1 is computed by column pivoting. For m>=1, r_m is the computed Ax_m-b, d_m is the column-pivoted computed value of A^-1 r_m, and x_(m+1) is the floating-point subtraction x_m-d_m. The conventions are x_0=0, r_0=-b, d_0=-x_1. Residual subtraction is last; s.p.r.a. uses single precision, while d.p.r.a. uses double precision followed by conversion to single precision.
The paper defines q_(m+1)=A(x_m-d_m)-b as the exact residual of x_m-d_m and bounds it for every m>=0. It defines bar_u=u for s.p.r.a. and bar_u=u^2 for d.p.r.a.
The Note defines c_3,c_4,c_5,C_6,C_7. Lemma 4.2 gives both a bound on |A(x_(m+1)-x)| and a bound on |x_(m+1)-x| in terms of |q_(m+1)|.

source_evidence.anchor: Lemma 4.3, following Note, and proof recurrence
source_evidence.observation: Lemma 4.3 states a four-term componentwise finite bound for |q_(m+1)| for every m>=0 under c_8*u*kappa(A^-1) <= 1/2. The Note defines C_8,c_8,C_9,C_10,C_11,C_12, and the proof records a one-step recurrence and a separate m=0 base case.

binders: n is the positive-integer system dimension; A is an n by n real matrix, b is an n-vector, and x=A^-1 b is the exact solution, so nonsingularity of A is inherited. [PDF p. 3 (printed 818), anchor: Section 2 opening; PDF p. 8 (printed 823), anchor: equation (3.1)]

u>0 is the single-precision relative-roundoff bound, and one residual variant, s.p.r.a. or d.p.r.a., is fixed; that choice determines bar_u. [PDF p. 3 (printed 818), anchor: floating-point model; PDF p. 10 (printed 825), anchor: Lemma 4.1]
x_m,r_m,d_m are generated by the Section 4 algorithm, and q_(m+1) is defined from x_m and d_m. [PDF p. 9 (printed 824), anchor: Section 4 algorithm; PDF p. 10 (printed 825), anchor: Lemma 4.1]
The displayed quantifier is m=0,1,2,...; the surrounding section fixes the data, arithmetic variant, norm, and constants before this quantifier. [PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3]
hypotheses: The standing arithmetic model has relative roundoff at most u>0, n*u <= 0.01, and every referenced floating-point operation is well defined. [PDF p. 3 (printed 818), anchor: Section 2 floating-point model]
A is nonsingular and x=A^-1 b is the exact solution used in the bound. [PDF p. 8 (printed 823), anchor: equation (3.1)]

The iterates use Gaussian elimination with column pivoting and iterative refinement, with residual subtraction performed last in the selected s.p.r.a. or d.p.r.a. mode. [PDF p. 9 (printed 824), anchor: Section 4 algorithm and residual-precision paragraph]

The Lemma 4.3 smallness condition is c_8*u*kappa(A^-1) <= 1/2, where c_8=||C_8|| and kappa(A^-1)=|| |A| |A^-1| ||. [PDF p. 5 (printed 820), anchor: definition of kappa(A^-1); PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3 and following Note]
conclusions: For every m=0,1,2,..., componentwise: |q_(m+1)| <= (u C_8 |A| |A^-1|)^m u C_10 |A| |x| + n bar_u |A| |x| + u^2 C_11 |A| |x| + bar_u*u C_12 |A| |A^-1| |A| |x|. The matrix-product order and exponent m are part of the statement. [PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3]
definitions_and_conventions: The exact solution is x=A^-1 b; |v| and |A| denote entrywise absolute value, and inequalities between arrays are componentwise. [PDF p. 3 (printed 818), anchor: componentwise convention; PDF p. 8 (printed 823), anchor: equation (3.1)]

The algorithm is x_1=the value of A^-1 b computed by column pivoting; for m=1,2,..., r_m is the computed Ax_m-b, d_m is the value of A^-1 r_m computed by column pivoting, and x_(m+1) is the rounded subtraction x_m-d_m. [PDF p. 9 (printed 824), anchor: Section 4 algorithm]
The initialization convention is x_0=0, r_0=-b, d_0=-x_1. [PDF p. 9 (printed 824), anchor: Section 4 initialization]

q_(m+1)=A(x_m-d_m)-b is the exact residual before the rounded update; the subtraction in this definition is exact mathematical subtraction. [PDF p. 9 (printed 824), anchor: rounded update; PDF p. 10 (printed 825), anchor: definition of q_(m+1)]
bar_u=u for s.p.r.a. and bar_u=u^2 for d.p.r.a. [PDF p. 10 (printed 825), anchor: Lemma 4.1]

Lower-case c_j are scalars, upper-case C_j are matrices, and I is the conformable identity matrix. [PDF p. 7 (printed 822), anchor: anonymous-constant convention; PDF p. 8 (printed 823), anchor: Note after equation (3.1)]
implicit_context: [Inherited] Column pivoting is the partial-pivoting variant that chooses the largest element of the next column as pivot. [PDF p. 3 (printed 818), anchor: paragraph beginning 'In Section 3']

[Inherited] The norm appearing in c_1,c_8 and kappa is an arbitrary fixed normalized absolute norm extended to matrices, not a uniquely named norm. [PDF p. 4 (printed 819), anchor: absolute monotone norm convention]

[Inferred from conformability] x,b,x_m,r_m,d_m and q_(m+1) are n-vectors; A,A^-1,I and every upper-case C_j are n by n matrices; lower-case c_j,u and bar_u are scalars. [PDF p. 7 (printed 822), anchor: scalar/matrix convention; PDF p. 9 (printed 824), anchor: algorithm; PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3]
[Cross-referenced] Lemma 4.1 states |q_(m+1)| <= u C_6|A||x_m-x| + (n bar_u+c_3 u^2)|A||x| + bar_u*u C_7|A||A^-1||A||x| under c_1*u*kappa(A^-1) <= 1/2. [PDF p. 10 (printed 825), anchor: Lemma 4.1]
[Cross-referenced, both parts] Lemma 4.2 states |A(x_(m+1)-x)| <= (I+u|A||A^-1|)|q_(m+1)|+u|A||x| and |x_(m+1)-x| <= (1+u)|A^-1||q_(m+1)|+u|x|. [PDF p. 11 (printed 826), anchor: Lemma 4.2]

[Proof detail] Substitution yields |q_(m+1)| <= u C_8|A||A^-1||q_m| + n bar_u|A||x| + u^2 C_9|A||x| + bar_u*u C_7|A||A^-1||A||x|; the proof then uses Lemma 4.1 for the m=0 base and induction. [PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3 proof recurrence]
statement.algorithm_linkage: The result is specific to Gaussian elimination with column pivoting followed by iterative refinement. Both the initial solve and each correction solve use column pivoting; the update is rounded subtraction; only residual accumulation varies between s.p.r.a. and d.p.r.a. The exact q_(m+1) is an analytical residual, not an additional computed output. [PDF p. 9 (printed 824), anchor: Section 4 algorithm and residual-precision paragraph; PDF p. 10 (printed 825), anchor: definition of q_(m+1)]
numerical_model: Ordinary floating-point relative roundoff is bounded by u, with u>0 and n*u <= 0.01. [PDF p. 3 (printed 818), anchor: Section 2 floating-point model]

For s.p.r.a., residual computation is in single precision with subtraction last, and bar_u=u. [PDF p. 9 (printed 824), anchor: residual-precision paragraph; PDF p. 10 (printed 825), anchor: Lemma 4.1]

For d.p.r.a., residual computation is in double precision with subtraction last, followed by conversion to single precision; double roundoff is bounded by u^2, conversion relative error by u, and bar_u=u^2. [PDF p. 9 (printed 824), anchor: residual-precision paragraph; PDF p. 10 (printed 825), anchor: Lemma 4.1]
A computed column-pivoted solve is controlled by |A x_hat-b| <= u C_2|A||x| under its precursor smallness condition. [PDF p. 8 (printed 823), anchor: equation (3.1)]
error_notions: q_(m+1) is the exact residual A(x_m-d_m)-b of the exact pre-update vector x_m-d_m. [PDF p. 10 (printed 825), anchor: definition of q_(m+1)]

r_m is instead the computed residual value of Ax_m-b; Lemma 4.3 does not identify q_(m+1) with r_(m+1). [PDF p. 9 (printed 824), anchor: Section 4 algorithm; PDF p. 10 (printed 825), anchor: definition of q_(m+1)]
The conclusion is a componentwise residual bound, not itself a normwise residual bound, forward-error bound, or backward-error assertion. [PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3]
norms: The norm is absolute, || |v| ||=||v||, equivalently monotone under componentwise domination; it is normalized by ||e_j||=1 and extended to matrices. [PDF p. 4 (printed 819), anchor: absolute monotone norm convention]
kappa(A^-1)=|| |A| |A^-1| || is explicitly nonstandard and appears in the smallness condition. [PDF p. 5 (printed 820), anchor: definition of kappa(A^-1); PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3]

The main conclusion places no norm around q_(m+1); its absolute values and inequality are entrywise/componentwise. [PDF p. 3 (printed 818), anchor: componentwise convention; PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3]
constants_and_indexing: c_1=||C_1|| and C_2=(I-u C_1|A||A^-1|)^-1 C_1; equation (3.1) assumes c_1*u*kappa(A^-1) <= 1/2. [PDF p. 8 (printed 823), anchor: equation (3.1) and following Note]
For s.p.r.a., c_3=(1+u)((1+u)^n-1)/u^2-n/u and c_4=0. For d.p.r.a., c_3=(1+u)(1+u^2)((1+u^2)^n-1)/u^2-n and c_4=1+u. [PDF p. 11 (printed 826), anchor: Note following Lemma 4.1]
c_5=n+(c_3+c_4)u^2/bar_u; C_6=C_2+(1+c_5*bar_u/u)(I+u C_2|A||A^-1|); C_7=(n+c_3*u^2/bar_u)C_2. [PDF p. 11 (printed 826), anchor: Note following Lemma 4.1]
C_8=(1+u)C_6, c_8=||C_8||, and C_9=C_6+c_3 I. [PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Note following Lemma 4.3]
C_10=C_6+(n*bar_u/u+c_3*u)I+bar_u C_7|A||A^-1|. [PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Note following Lemma 4.3]
C_11=(I-u C_8|A||A^-1|)^-1 C_9 and C_12=(I-u C_8|A||A^-1|)^-1(n C_8+C_7); the noncommutative factor order is as printed. [PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Note following Lemma 4.3]
The paper states that the quantities C_8,c_8,C_9,C_10,C_11,C_12 are bounded above by functions of n only. [PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Note following Lemma 4.3]
The residual index is m+1 and the first term uses matrix exponent m. At m=0 the result concerns q_1 and the zeroth matrix power is the identity. [PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3 and proof]
higher_order_terms: Lemma 4.3 is a finite four-term inequality with no O(u^k) remainder. [PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3]

For s.p.r.a., the explicit second and fourth terms carry n*u and u^2; for d.p.r.a., they carry n*u^2 and u^3. The third term is explicitly u^2 in both variants. [PDF p. 10 (printed 825), anchor: definition of bar_u; PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3]
The iteration-dependent term remains exactly (u C_8|A||A^-1|)^m u C_10|A||x| rather than being replaced by asymptotic notation. [PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3]
exceptional_values: Every referenced floating-point operation is assumed well defined, and the floating-point set is a subset of the reals. [PDF p. 3 (printed 818), anchor: Section 2 floating-point model]
A^-1 is used throughout, so singular A lies outside the setting. [PDF p. 8 (printed 823), anchor: x=A^-1 b and equation (3.1)]

The definitions of C_2,C_11,C_12 contain matrix inverses and are used under the corresponding smallness assumptions; Lemma 4.3 adds no separate exceptional-value clause. [PDF p. 8 (printed 823), anchor: Note after equation (3.1); PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3 Note]

undebatable_constraints: The target is q_(m+1)=A(x_m-d_m)-b, the exact residual before the rounded update, not r_m, r_(m+1), or A x_(m+1)-b. [PDF p. 10 (printed 825), anchor: definition of q_(m+1)]
The result applies for every integer m>=0, with q_1 corresponding to m=0 and the geometric matrix factor raised to exactly m. [PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3]
All four additive terms must be preserved, including n*bar_u|A||x|, u^2 C_11|A||x|, and bar_u*u C_12|A||A^-1||A||x|. [PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3]

The smallness condition is c_8*u*kappa(A^-1) <= 1/2, with c_8=||C_8|| and the paper's nonstandard kappa(A^-1)=|| |A| |A^-1| ||. [PDF p. 5 (printed 820), anchor: kappa definition; PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3 and Note]
bar_u=u for s.p.r.a. and bar_u=u^2 for d.p.r.a. [PDF p. 10 (printed 825), anchor: Lemma 4.1]

The conclusion is componentwise and uses ordered matrix products; replacing it by only a norm inequality changes the claim. [PDF p. 3 (printed 818), anchor: componentwise convention; PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3]

Upper-case C_8,C_10,C_11,C_12 are matrices, while lower-case c_8 is a scalar norm. [PDF p. 7 (printed 822), anchor: anonymous-constant convention; PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Note following Lemma 4.3]
Both the initial and correction solves use Gaussian elimination with column pivoting. [PDF p. 9 (printed 824), anchor: Section 4 algorithm]
Residual accumulation retains the subtraction-last rule and the distinct single- and double-precision models. [PDF p. 9 (printed 824), anchor: residual-precision paragraph]
No big-O remainder may replace the explicit u^2 and bar_u*u terms. [PDF p. 12 (printed 827), anchor: Lemma 4.3]

contract_plain_english: For a nonsingular real n by n system Ax=b, run the paper's column-pivoted Gaussian-elimination iterative refinement, computing residuals with subtraction last and choosing either single-precision residual accumulation (bar_u=u) or double-precision accumulation followed by single conversion (bar_u=u^2). Let q_(m+1)=A(x_m-d_m)-b be the exact residual of the pre-rounded corrected vector. Under the standing roundoff assumptions and c_8*u*|| |A| |A^-1| || <= 1/2, every m>=0 satisfies the exact four-term componentwise bound |q_(m+1)| <= (u C_8|A||A^-1|)^m u C_10|A||x| + n bar_u|A||x| + u^2 C_11|A||x| + bar_u*u C_12|A||A^-1||A||x|, with C_8 through C_12 defined by the paper's Notes. No term is an omitted big-O remainder, q is not the computed residual r, and the norm in the smallness condition is any fixed normalized absolute norm allowed by the paper. [PDF p. 3 (printed 818), anchor: floating-point conventions; PDF p. 4 (printed 819), anchor: norm convention; PDF p. 5 (printed 820), anchor: kappa definition; PDF p. 9 (printed 824), anchor: Section 4 algorithm; PDF pp. 10-12 (printed 825-827), anchors: Lemmas 4.1-4.3]
